name: ldbc_mix
title: LDBC Interactive, LDBC frequencies (sf3's)
sweep_marks: the driver's time pacing (0.62x the reads)
method: LDBC's driver config and sf3 update stream (python/kvevaluator/workloads/interactive/gen_ldbc_mix.py). Complex reads IC1-IC12: one run per freq_i updates (sf3.properties; IC13/IC14 have no plans here). Short reads IS1-IS7: the driver's random walk after EVERY complex read, IC13/IC14 included (1.255 runs of each IS per complex read, 0.370 complex reads per update; an upper bound -- a walk that finds no ids ends early). Updates IU1-IU8: their shares of the sf3 update stream. Frequencies are the benchmark's stated intent: the driver paces reads by time, and on these stream files it would issue ~0.62x the complex reads per update -- the write:read sweep covers that range. The sf3 prescription is used at every SF.
expect: Condensed props (IS1/IS4/IS5 read whole vertices; IU inserts write whole vertices). Lists split by edge type: knows (read by most ICs, written by IU8 only, 1% of updates) Condensed or Chunked; the write-heavy lists -- hasMember (IU5, 49% of updates), likes (IU2/IU3, 29%), the Comment/Post edges (IU6/IU7) -- Split in bytes. So the best MIXED layout should beat every uniform one on at least one currency without losing the other (a real test of the rule: parts carry different traffic). IC5 reads hasMember, so hasMember is the contested part.
